questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I had to choose my study destination I considered the quality of the University, the city's reputation and the social and academic life on campus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
UCC is a great university with enthusiastic professors. They have a lot of courses within different areas. Besides the academics, they have a lot of societies and clubs. This made the experience even more greater. 
Cork city was a great smaller city with a lot of coffee shops and restaurants. Outside cork was the most fascinating and breathtaking nature, which is definitely work exploring.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon my arrival I was sent a lot of information on what to do and when. They also sent out mails reminding us of the deadlines.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The international office assisted us upon arrival. There was an academic and social introduction lecture and campus tours.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not that easy. I was very lucky and lived at Brookefield village- a student accommodation. Here I lived with 7 other persons in a house. This was just next to campus but 30 min from the city center on foot. I now that a lot of people struggled to find accommodation. beside that is the accommodation very overpriced.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be very difficult, so start looking for accommodation the minute you get accepted by KU. Be prepared that it is very expensive to rent a place in Cork

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to choose the courses we wanted through a portal, which worked very good. But we had to register very late, which was a bit stressful, since you could not be sure if you got accepted for the class

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international officie. They were very busy and therefore not very good at replying. This whole process of registering for courses was a bit of a mess and chaotic.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It got accepted for 4 out of 6, which meant I had to find some other classes which was a bit stressfull, but everything was sorted out in the end. The international office helped a lot.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the documents you are send carefully

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was the same as KU. We had to learn everything by heart, which was a bit different than from KU. The professors were nice to answer questions and help the international students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
More learn by
heart.They
mostly only had lectures and not any seminars, where you are in smaller groups answering questions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: The humane nervous system, neuropharmacology, pharmacology,  advanced methodology neuroscience and introduction to neuroscience.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The pharmacology and neuropharmacology had great professors. They were so enthusiastic and really cared about the lectures they gave. The topics in the courses were very relevant for my studies and were super interesting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were more than 100 societies and 50 clubs. The university has a very big arena with fitness, swimming pool and other sports.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of things they had everything from a knitting society to harry potter society. They also had environmental society, STEM society etc. They also had many sport clubs - both traditional irish sport clubs and international sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for a lot of societies and clubs- you meet a lot of great people and learn a lot.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking! Ireland have the most amazing nature

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! The people are super friendly and helpful!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Engage in the societies and clubs

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Accept that things does not work as fast as in Denmark. The irish people are generally more chilled

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people and how helpful they were.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Participate in a lot of things
Try not to stress about the things you cant affect
Read up on the area where you are gonna live - what is there to see etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring rain clothes and hiking boots.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
All the amazing friends I made while on exchange. 
The academic aspect also made the experience incredibly

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Choosing the courses and navigating through the universities world.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun! Enjoy while you are there and get the most of it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
